During a public address in Banaskantha, Gujarat, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the disbursement of the latest instalment of the PM Kisan Samman Nidhi, transferring over 18,000 crore rupees to around 10 crore farmers across India. He highlighted that government initiatives such as subsidized fertilizers, MSP procurement, PM Fasal Bima Yojana, and the PM KUSUM solar scheme have cumulatively benefited farmers with over 50 lakh crore rupees in savings and transfers. The Prime Minister underscored technological advancements in agriculture and animal husbandry, citing the distribution of over 26 crore Soil Health Cards, breed conservation via IVF, and nationwide cattle vaccination drives. He also dedicated and laid the foundation stones for key infrastructure projects, including two new train services, the Ahmedabad Metro extension to GIFT City and the airport, highway widening, cluster development programmes for horticulture, and modern Anganwadis across Gujarat, while inviting citizens to join the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations. UP's 1090 Women Powerline: Tackling Harassment, FFR Method, & 30-Day Follow-Up
In Uttar Pradesh, the Women Powerline 1090 serves as a crucial support channel for women facing harassment over phone calls or social media. Upon receiving a complaint, police initiate action by issuing a warning call directly to the accused. If the misconduct persists, authorities employ the Family, Friends, and Relatives technique to contact close associates of the offender. Operating through a 150-seat call centre handling approximately 8,000 incoming and 10,000 outgoing calls daily, the helpline also offers emotional support and counselling to complainants. To guarantee long-term safety, police conduct a follow-up 30 days after action is taken, reopening the resolution process if harassment continues.
PM Modi Slams Opposition in Banaskantha Over Anarchy, Launches Rs 14,400-Crore Projects
Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched development projects worth approximately 14,400 crore rupees in Banaskantha, Gujarat, reflecting on his 25-year political journey from the state. In his address, he launched a sharp attack against the opposition, accusing them of spreading fake narratives about shortages of gas and urea amid global supply disruptions caused by the US-Iran conflict. He stated that these narratives were designed to gain control and spread anarchy across the country. Modi affirmed that the government ensured uninterrupted urea supplies at existing rates and resolved to serve the public until his last breath, with plans to announce an additional 19,000 crore rupees under the PM-Kisan scheme.
MSP, Solar Pumps and Dairy Sector: Boost for Farmers Across India
A public address detailed government initiatives supporting farmers and transforming the rural economy across the country. Amid rising global fertiliser costs, nearly 16 lakh crore rupees were spent to shield agriculturalists from price spikes, alongside distributing over 24 lakh crore rupees under minimum support price schemes for wheat and paddy over the last twelve years. More than two lakh crore rupees have been disbursed under the PM Fasal Bima Yojana, while around 12 lakh solar pumps sanctioned under the PM-KUSUM scheme saved over 80 crore litres of diesel. Science and technology have also been introduced into daily farming, with 26 crore Soil Health Cards and nearly 3,000 climate-resilient seed varieties distributed. Furthermore, dairy and animal husbandry sectors received significant support through the Rashtriya Gokul Mission, free vaccination drives administering nearly 150 crore doses, and scientific breeding techniques, boosting average daily milk output from under five litres in 2013-14 to nearly eight litres.
Supreme Court Cancels Anand Singh's Bail, Sets December 1 Surrender Deadline
In a major setback to expelled Janata Dal (United) legislator Anand Singh, the Supreme Court has directed him to surrender by December 1. Singh, an accused in the 2025 Dulare Chand Yadav murder case, had earlier been granted bail by the Patna High Court. That decision was challenged before the top court through a petition seeking the cancellation of his bail. The Supreme Court rejected relief for the Mokama legislator, setting an ultimatum for him to return to custody by the stipulated deadline while further details of the order are awaited.
